# AGENTS.md

Instructions for coding agents working on this repository, the Next.js SaaS Starter with PostgreSQL and Stripe. A Next.js 16 SaaS starter kit in TypeScript with PostgreSQL, Better Auth, Drizzle ORM, Tailwind CSS and shadcn/ui. It is a free, MIT-licensed SaaS boilerplate for developers who want sign-up and sign-in, teams with roles, onboarding, Stripe subscriptions, an admin panel, API keys and a REST API already built. It runs with no third-party keys: email, billing and social sign-in switch on when you add their variables.

## Install and run

You need Node.js 22.12 or newer and Docker (for a local PostgreSQL).

```bash
docker run -d --name saas-db -p 5432:5432 -e POSTGRES_PASSWORD=postgres postgres:16
cp .env.example .env.local     # then set AUTH_SECRET, e.g. to the output of: openssl rand -hex 32
npm install
npm run dev                    # applies migrations, then starts Next.js
```

Open <http://localhost:3000> and sign up: the first account is the admin. Until you set `RESEND_API_KEY`, emails (verification, reset, invites) are printed in the terminal.

## Test

```bash
npm run lint
npm run typecheck
npm test                       # unit tests, plus the integration test when DATABASE_URL is set
npm run build && npm start     # then, in another terminal:
npm run smoke                  # checks a running app, BASE_URL=http://localhost:3000 by default
```

The integration test signs up two users, creates their workspaces and API keys, and drives the REST API: create, read, update, delete, workspace isolation, plan limit and bad keys.

CI (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`) runs on every push and pull request: lint, typecheck, test, build. The `main` branch requires it to pass.

## Deploy with the Light Cloud MCP server

The [Light Cloud MCP server](https://docs.light-cloud.com/deploy-with-ai/mcp-server) (`@light-cloud/mcp-server` on npm) lets you deploy this folder and keep changing it from a conversation. Add it once:

```bash
claude mcp add light-cloud -- npx -y @light-cloud/mcp-server   # Claude Code
```

Cursor, VS Code with GitHub Copilot and Claude Desktop take the same command (`npx -y @light-cloud/mcp-server`) in their MCP settings: see https://docs.light-cloud.com/deploy-with-ai/mcp-server. Then:

1. `connect` with your email (it creates the account when there is none) or `login`.
2. `create-database`, then `get-database-connection-string`, then `set-environment-variables` with the database variables this app reads (see `.env.example`).
3. `detect-local-framework` on this folder, then `upload-and-deploy`; or `create-application` from your GitHub copy of this repository.
4. `wait-for-deployment` returns the live URL. If the build fails, `get-build-logs` shows why; `get-environment-logs` shows the running app's logs.

Without an agent, follow part 1 of the series: https://blog.light-cloud.com/tutorials/start-a-saas-part-1-deploy

## Project rules

- It is a template people deploy with no setup: it must install, start and pass its tests with the values in `.env.example` and no third-party keys. Optional integrations switch on only when their variables are set.
- The server listens on the port in `PORT`, and every database setting comes from the environment variables in `.env.example`, which Light Cloud sets on deploy. Never hard-code credentials.
- There is no Light Cloud-specific code in it, and there should not be: it must keep running on any host (README.md › Deploy anywhere else).
- Use npm: `package-lock.json` is committed, so add packages with `npm install <package>` and commit the lockfile.
- Every page checks its own access (`requireWorkspace()`, or the platform-admin check in `/admin`), not only its layout: Next.js renders a layout and its page in parallel, so a layout check alone does not stop the page's data being sent.
- Add or update tests with each change, and run the commands under Test before you finish.
- README.md is the template's landing page. Keep its H1, badges and Deploy button. The blocks between `<!-- header:start -->`, `<!-- stack:start -->` and `<!-- faq:start -->` markers, this file's generated block, CI and the dev container are generated from `catalogue.json` in [awesome-templates](https://github.com/light-cloud-dev/awesome-templates): change them there. Keep the rest of the README in step with the code.
- Note user-facing changes under `## [Unreleased]` in CHANGELOG.md.
- Copy is UK English, sentence case, no emoji.

## Environment variables

| Name | Required | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `DATABASE_URL` | Yes | none | PostgreSQL connection URL. Set by Light Cloud. |
| `AUTH_SECRET` | Yes | none | Signs sessions and email tokens. Generated by Light Cloud at deploy. |
| `PORT` | No | `3000` | Port to listen on. Set by Light Cloud. |
| `APP_URL` | No | from each request | Public URL. Set it when you add a custom domain. |
| `APP_NAME` | No | `Your App` | Product name in the header, titles and emails. |
| `ADMIN_EMAILS` | No | empty | Comma-separated emails that are admins, on top of the first user. |
| `RESEND_API_KEY` | No | empty | Sends email through Resend and turns on email verification. |
| `EMAIL_FROM` | No | `Your App <onboarding@resend.dev>` | Sender, on a domain verified in Resend. |
| `GITHUB_CLIENT_ID`, `GITHUB_CLIENT_SECRET` | No | empty | Turn on GitHub sign-in (both needed). |
| `GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID`, `GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET` | No | empty | Turn on Google sign-in (both needed). |
| `STRIPE_SECRET_KEY`, `STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET`, `STRIPE_PRICE_PRO`, `STRIPE_PRICE_BUSINESS` | No | empty | Turn on billing (all four needed): API key, webhook signing secret, monthly price ids. |

None of these reach the browser. Change a variable on Light Cloud, then redeploy. Set `APP_URL` once you know your domain, so email links never depend on request headers.

## Project structure

```text
.
├── src/
│   ├── app/
│   │   ├── (marketing)/       # /, /pricing, /terms, /privacy
│   │   ├── (auth)/            # /sign-in, /sign-up, /forgot-password, /reset-password, /invite/[id]
│   │   ├── (app)/             # /dashboard, /projects, /settings/*, /workspaces/new
│   │   ├── onboarding/        # first-time setup stepper
│   │   ├── admin/             # /admin, platform admins only
│   │   └── api/               # auth/[...all] (Better Auth, Stripe webhook), health, v1/projects
│   ├── components/            # app shell, forms, dialogs; ui/ holds shadcn/ui components
│   └── lib/                   # auth, config, plans, permissions, billing, email, api-keys, projects, db/
├── drizzle/                   # SQL migrations (committed)
├── scripts/                   # migrate.mjs (run by npm start) and smoke.mjs
├── test/                      # Vitest unit and integration tests
└── .env.example               # every environment variable, explained
```
